title: Angeline the Baker
short: Traditional (American) · C 4/4 · play it with every note lit.

blocks.html: A gentle, singing old-time tune, a favorite at jams because the melody is plain and lovely. It sits well in double C tuning (g C G C D): most notes are open strings or the 2nd fret. Every finger stroke falls on a beat; the eighth notes between come from the thumb (on the 5th string, or dropped onto the 3rd string) or from a hammer-on with the left hand. Fiddlers play it in D: put a capo at the 2nd fret (and raise the 5th string to A) to play along with them.

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys or strings light up as each note sounds.

blocks.html: The piece: Old-time fiddle tune; the title comes from Stephen Foster’s song “Angelina Baker” (1850)

sources.name: Melody checked note by note against an ABC transcription of “Angeline the Baker” (in D) in John Chambers’s tune collection at MIT (trillian.mit.edu), moved down a step to C and an octave lower. We leave out the pickup notes and start on the downbeat. Every melody note of that version is in our tab at its time (one high G is played on the 5th string, an octave up). Chords are ours. History of the title from Wikipedia.
